sections.h2: Ways to sell a Cedar Park house
sections.html:
A Cedar Park owner can work with an agent, manage the sale personally, or accept an investor's cash purchase with no repairs. Condition and timing decide which suits you.

  • With an agent: broad buyer exposure, plus showings, lender appraisals and post-inspection repair requests.
  • Self-managed: you price the house and coordinate the contract with a title company.
  • Investor purchase: built for deferred maintenance, occupied rentals, estates or a tight calendar.

Three Cedar Park items come up in nearly every sale: the permit record, any short-term rental registration, and the tax account.

Cedar Park is a Williamson County city that grew from a ranch settlement into an Austin suburb and incorporated in 1973. Its economic development group calls it the third largest city in the Austin metro. Most sale questions here concern current permits, registrations and tax accounts rather than old title tangles.

sections.h2: Which appraisal district and tax office apply?
sections.html:
Your latest tax statement names the county and the appraisal district that carry your parcel. Cedar Park is part of Williamson County, whose Central Appraisal District values property there.

Texas levies no state property tax, so each local unit sets its own rate. Value is set on January 1, the year's lien attaches that day, and bills follow in October. Tax unpaid after January 31 turns delinquent on February 1, and penalty and interest begin to build. For current rates, call the Williamson County tax office and ask for each unit's rate on your bill.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and the 10 percent cap
sections.html:
Cedar Park homeowners get a brake on rising assessments, and it stays with the owner, not the house. Williamson CAD says a home qualifies in the second full year the exemption has been on the property for the same owner. After that, increases in existing assessed value are held to 10 percent a year even when market value climbs faster.

The cap doesn't transfer with ownership, so a buyer starts fresh and may see a bigger jump than you did. Tell a buyer to budget for that jump. Other points from the district:

  • You apply once, and the exemption stays unless you move or add another one.
  • A Texas driver license or ID showing your current address is required.
  • Processing can take up to 90 days.
  • The chief appraiser re-checks each homestead exemption within every five tax years.

If your Cedar Park house is rented for stays of 30 consecutive days or fewer, the city's April 2026 ordinance applies. Registration is required, costs $100 a year, and ties into Hotel Occupancy Tax reporting under Chapter 10 of the City Code. The city estimates about 200 active short-term rentals.

A buyer who plans to keep renting will ask whether the registration exists and whether tax was remitted. Development Services at 512-401-5100 handles registration, and Utility Billing at 512-401-5300 handles hotel tax payments. Registered owners can watch remittance through an online portal. Gather the confirmation and remittance history before you list, since a rental buyer asks for them first.

sections.h2: Permits and repairs to check before you sell
sections.html:
Open permits are a common reason a Cedar Park closing pauses. The city runs permits through the MGO Connect portal, and Development Services is at the City Hall campus, 450 Cypress Creek Road, Building 1. Its zoning map tool, CPAtlas, lets you type in an address to see zoning.

Cedar Park permit timing and rules
Permit topicRule
Typical residential permit timeGenerally 5 to 7 business days
Permit expiryLapses if not issued, or work not started, within 180 days; also after 180 days of stopped work
Inspection requestsMade before 3 pm go on the next business day's schedule; same day not guaranteed
Owner-pulled electrical, mechanical or plumbing permitNeeds a homeowner affidavit and proof of homestead exemption

To reopen or cancel a permit, email permits@cedarparktexas.gov with the status of the project, and the city will review and reply. Inspection notes sit on the permit record in the portal, so you can print them for the buyer.

Each situation runs on a Texas clock.

  • Foreclosure: the borrower gets 20 days from the default notice to reinstate, and auctions take place at the courthouse on first Tuesdays.
  • Inheritance: a will can be probated for four years after death, and the small estate affidavit tops out at $75,000 excluding homestead and exempt property.
  • Tenant: a landlord normally gives 3 days of written notice to vacate before filing in justice court, unless the lease sets another period.

A buyer can take on these issues, but the title company still needs proof of who may sign. A Williamson County probate attorney can say which paper fits. If more than one of these applies, tell every buyer at the start, so nobody is surprised once the title search is under way.

The city says the registration lets it count and locate short-term rentals, support safety, and make sure hotel tax is collected. For you as a seller that translates into a paper trail. A buyer who reviews your account will see whether the house was registered, whether hotel tax was remitted and when. Missing months are easier to fix before a contract than during one, so check the portal now rather than after you have an offer.

sections.h2: How an open permit slows a closing
sections.html:
A title company or a buyer's inspector who finds an unfinished project, such as a deck, a water heater swap or a remodel, will ask whether it was permitted and closed. The permit record answers that. If the permit shows work that never started or that stopped, it may lapse after 180 days, and getting it reopened takes a request by email with the project status. Printing the inspection notes from the portal gives the buyer a clear picture, and the cash buyer can then decide what to do about anything left open.

An owner who pulled a permit without a contractor should be able to show the homeowner affidavit and proof of homestead that the city required. Keep those with the rest of the closing folder.

Do these in order and you will know which sale routes are open.

  • Pull the tax statement and confirm the district and any balance.
  • Ask Development Services whether any permit on the address is open.
  • Get your mortgage payoff figure.
  • If the house was a short-term rental, collect registration and hotel tax records.
  • Name your deadline, such as a sale date or a move, and tell every buyer about it.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Cedar Park house with an open building permit?
faqs.a: Yes, though it complicates the sale. A permit lapses after 180 days without a start or with work stopped. Call Development Services at 512-401-5100 about the record, or sell to a buyer willing to take the open item.

faqs.q: Must my Cedar Park short-term rental be registered before a sale?
faqs.a: If guests stay 30 days or fewer, registration is required at $100 a year. A buyer planning to keep renting will want the registration and your hotel occupancy tax records.

faqs.q: Does my homestead tax cap pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Williamson CAD says the cap does not transfer with ownership. The new owner applies for an exemption of their own, and the cap counts from their first full year.

faqs.q: When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: Tax unpaid after January 31 is delinquent on February 1. Call the Williamson County tax office for the exact balance on your account.

faqs.q: What does the Texas foreclosure timeline look like?
faqs.a: A default notice starts a 20-day reinstatement window. The lender then gives notice of sale, and the auction happens at the courthouse on a first Tuesday.
